transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Hello! I'm Dora, and I'm here to help answer any questions you might have about your cataract surgery or your recovery. 

Do you have any questions for me today?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hi Dora, yes, I do have a few questions. First, when can I start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Great! So for gardening, you can start doing light gardening after 1 week following your surgery. That's perfectly fine to do.

However, you should avoid any strenuous or heavy exercise for about a month after your operation.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thanks for that information. My next question is, when can I start using my eye gel for dry eyes?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Good question. If you were using eye gel for dry eyes before your operation, it's safe to continue using it unless you've been told otherwise by your care team.

So you can go ahead and use it as you were before. If you're running out and need more, your GP should be able to provide some.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: That’s helpful, thank you. I'm also finding that I'm very sensitive to bright light. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.intended:
Yes, that is quite normal. It's common for your eyes to be a bit sensitive to light as they adjust to your new lenses.

If it's mild and things just seem brighter than you're used to, I'd recommend wearing sunglasses when you're outside.

However, if you have significant pain when it's bright, or severe light sensitivity - especially if your eye is also red and painful - that's not normal and we may need to check that further.

Do you have any other questions?
transcript.delivered: Yes, that is quite normal. It's common for your eyes to be a bit sensitive to light as they adjust to your new lenses.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Oh, I see. But should I still have some blurriness by now?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
It's common for vision to not be completely clear in the first week after your operation, but it should improve quickly and settle down over time.

How long ago was your surgery? If your vision is still quite blurry or getting significantly worse, we may need to check it to make sure everything is okay.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thanks for explaining. I had my surgery about a week ago, so hopefully it clears up soon. I appreciate all the information. I don't have any more questions right now.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: That's great! So just to confirm - have all your questions been answered today?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, all my questions have been answered. Thanks for your help!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're very welcome! Take care, and best of luck with your recovery.

verdict.label: fail
verdict.reasoning: The agent conveyed `normal_sensitivity_reassurance` when Dora stated, "Yes, that is quite normal. It's common for your eyes to be a bit sensitive to light as they adjust to your new lenses." However, the agent was interrupted and did not convey `escalation_criteria` or `mild_case_advice`.
